name: Fleet Monitor
description: System monitor for Orca: live CPU usage, per-core load and memory usage (RAM, swap, memory pressure) for this computer and all your paired remote servers. Like an activity monitor or task manager for all your machines: performance monitoring, stats and system resources in one sidebar panel.

commands.title: Fleet Monitor: Send a test alert

settings.title: Fast interval (seconds)
settings.description: How often machines are read while a Fleet Monitor panel is open.

settings.title: Slow interval (seconds)
settings.description: How often machines are read for the status bar while no panel is open, when background monitoring is on.

settings.title: RAM used busy at (%)
settings.description: For machines that report real RAM usage (Macs running Fleet Monitor 1.1 or later): RAM in use, as Activity Monitor counts it, at which the machine counts as busy.

settings.title: Orca CLI path
settings.description: Leave empty to find the CLI that ships with this Orca.

settings.title: Publish this machine's readings
settings.description: Write a short reading to this plugin's log every 5 seconds, so a paired desktop can show per-core CPU for this machine. On a Mac it also publishes the names and owners of that machine's top processes, about every 30 seconds.

settings.title: Monitor in the background
settings.description: Read machines on the slow interval while no Fleet Monitor panel is open, to keep the status bar current and to send memory alerts for paired machines. Off, paired machines are read, and alert, only while a Fleet Monitor panel is open here; this computer still alerts. Turn it off on a machine that is there to publish its readings: it keeps publishing.

settings.title: Alert when memory runs short
settings.description: Show a desktop notification when a machine's memory reaches critical (on its first reading) or strained (two readings in a row), with a reminder every 10 minutes while it stays critical, and when a machine stops answering while its memory is short.
